subtitle: What happens after a task fails — and how to control it

eyebrow: What a real failure actually looks like
caption: A genuine exception and traceback — retries decide what happens next, not what gets logged.

code:
load_to_snowflake = SQLExecuteQueryOperator(
    task_id="load_to_snowflake",
    conn_id="snowflake_default",
    sql="copy_into_raw_sales.sql",
    retries=3,
    retry_delay=timedelta(minutes=5),
)
caption: Try up to 3 more times, waiting 5 minutes between attempts.

code:
load_to_snowflake = SQLExecuteQueryOperator(
    task_id="load_to_snowflake",
    retries=5,
    retry_delay=timedelta(minutes=2),
    retry_exponential_backoff=True,
    max_retry_delay=timedelta(minutes=30),
)
caption: Each retry waits longer than the last, capped at 30 minutes.

code:
def notify_data_team(context):
    task_id = context["task_instance"].task_id
    dag_id = context["dag"].dag_id
    print(f"{dag_id}.{task_id} failed.")

load_to_snowflake = SQLExecuteQueryOperator(
    task_id="load_to_snowflake",
    on_failure_callback=notify_data_team,
)
caption: Runs once, only after every retry is exhausted.
